You are assembling a clinical visit note. The sentences of one note are listed below in random order with their section headings removed. File every sentence under one of these four headings: SUBJECTIVE, OBJECTIVE EXAM, OBJECTIVE RESULTS, ASSESSMENT AND PLAN. In the JSON, the headings are the keys subjective, objective_exam, objective_results and assessment_and_plan. Return each sentence ID under exactly one heading. Do not leave any sentence out and do not invent IDs.

<sentences>
S1: For his diabetes, he stated that he has been measuring his blood glucose levels 4 to 5 times per week, but I want him to start measuring them 2 to 3 times per day.
S2: As far as treatment, he has been elevating his knee and taking Tylenol without significant relief of his pain.
S3: He explains that he was jumping on a trampoline when he heard a snap, followed by instant pain in the lateral aspect of his knee.
S4: William Russell is a pleasant 57-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of a right knee injury.
S5: I'm going to order an echocardiogram for further evaluation, but I want him to continue taking his lisinopril 20 mg for now.
S6: In terms of his hypertension, the patient admits that he did not purchase a blood pressure cuff as previously recommended.
S7: He has also been taking his metformin 500 mg as prescribed.
S8: I also put in a referral for physical therapy so he can work on strengthening the muscles around the area and prevent any further injury.
S9: While he does not monitor his blood pressures at home, he has been compliant with lisinopril 20 mg.
S10: Ecchymosis and edema along the lateral aspect.
S11: MSK: Examination of the right knee: Mild tenderness to palpation at the lateral aspect.
S12: For his hypertension, I'm concerned that his blood pressure is not well controlled at this time, so we may need to modify his medication.
S13: He has not tried applying heat or ice to the area.
S14: I'm also going to order a lipid panel and we can determine if any adjustments need to be made to his medication.
S15: Decent range of motion.
S16: His diabetes appears to be stable based on home monitoring, although he is only checking his blood glucose levels 4 to 5 times per week.
S17: CV: Regular rate and rhythm.
S18: Musculoskeletal: Reports right knee pain.
S19: After reviewing the patient's examination and radiographic findings today, his symptoms appear to be consistent with a lateral ligament strain of the right knee.
S20: I am going to prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily for pain and swelling.
S21: In the meantime, he should continue taking metformin 500 mg.
S22: These reveal no evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.
S23: Lungs are clear bilaterally.
S24: He has a past medical history significant for hypertension and type 2 diabetes.
S25: X-rays of the right knee were obtained and reviewed.
S26: Right knee pain, lateral ligament strain.
S27: He does not follow any specific diet plan, but he does try to make healthier choices such as limiting his carbohydrate intake.
S28: His hemoglobin A1c levels should provide more detail as far as his long-term progress so we will order that today.
S29: This is not a common activity for him, and he admits that he is inconsistent with exercise.
S30: Approximately 1 week ago, the patient sustained an injury to his right knee while at a trampoline park.
S31: We can consider further imaging if he continues to have pain, but I explained that this is a common injury that typically heals on it's own.
</sentences>
